div.head: Abt 6
div.ab: Gif man frigne mannan ofsleahþ, cyninge L scill' to drihtinbeage.
Gif man frigne mannan of sleahþ, cyninge L scilƚ to drihtinbeage.
If a person kills a free man, 50 shillings to the king as lord-payment.
If a man slays a free man, he shall pay 50 shillings to the king for infraction of his seignorial rights.
If anyone kills a freeman, [he is to pay] 50 shillings to the king as “lordring”.
Wenn jemand einen freien Mann erschlägt, [büsse er] dem Könige 50 Schill. zum Herrschergeld.
If someone slays a free man, [let him pay] the king 50 shillings as lord’s payment.
div.note: Presumably what is called elsewhere a manbot. The term used here is obviously ancient, belonging to a time when payments were more often in rings than in currency. Several of the words in this code are either unique, or used otherwise only in poetry, which was conservative in its vocabulary.
